Crucially, although turbidity correlates with titer overall (pooled r=-0.65), when FWF is held fixed the turbidity->titer relationship collapses (slope goes from -0.29/-0.26 at high FWF to -0.06/-0.003 at low FWF, p up to 0.90). That is the fingerprint of a bystander: FWF simultaneously drives both cloudiness and titer loss, so once FWF is controlled, turbidity carries essentially no independent effect. Temperature and DO were ruled out (stable/no effect), and the metal-chelating additive is not available on this line. Decisive test: holding FWF constant eliminated the turbidity-titer link, proving turbidity is a confounded decoy and feed-water flow is the true cause. Fix: reduce feed-water flow to zero (or minimum), which maximized titer; investigate the replaced fitting as the ingress source.
